title: Wall ahead. Brake or swerve? Braking needs 12.3 m, a full swerve 24.6 m, twice as far
description:
Wall ahead. Brake or swerve? Two cars side by side at 50 km/h (13.8889 m/s) with the same grip, 0.8 g = 7.8453 m/s^2 in any direction (a friction circle, g = 9.80665 m/s^2). A wall spans the whole road 15 m ahead. No reaction time: both act at t = 0. Left, brake: straight at the full grip. Right, swerve: the full grip sideways, no braking, so the car runs on a circle of radius v^2 / (mu g) at a constant 50 km/h. Each car is a point, the centre of its front bumper, drawn as a 4.5 x 1.8 m body. Both integrated by RK4 at 12000 steps per second with the stop and the hit located by bisection inside the step, checked against the closed forms and a half-step rerun, shown at 1/3 speed on a 38 s loop. Deterministic, no seed.

Measured:
- braking stops in 12.2940 m after 1.7703 s (closed forms v^2 / (2 mu g) and v / (mu g)), 2.7060 m short of the wall
- the swerving car keeps 50.00 km/h at every step and runs on a circle of radius 24.5881 m (closed form v^2 / (mu g)), 2.0000 times the braking distance
- to stop moving toward a wall across the whole road, the swerve must turn a full quarter turn: 24.5881 m forward after 2.7808 s, 9.5881 m more than the 15 m to the wall
- so the swerve hits the wall at 1.1616 s, turned 37.59 degrees (asin(15 / R)), 5.105 m to the side, still at 50.00 km/h, 39.62 km/h of it square to the wall; at that moment the braking car is 10.840 m from the line at 17.19 km/h, and it stops 0.6088 s later
- brake to a speed u, then turn at full grip: the forward distance is v^2 / (2 mu g) + u^2 / (2 mu g), so 12.2940 m for u = 0 km/h, 12.7858 m for 10, 14.2611 m for 20, 16.7199 m for 30, 20.1622 m for 40, 24.5881 m for 50; pure braking is the shortest
- at 70 km/h: braking 24.0963 m in 2.4785 s, a full swerve 48.1926 m, again 2.0000 times
- a narrow obstacle is different: a 2 m sidestep needs only 9.7135 m forward (sqrt(2 R s - s^2)), less than the 12.2940 m braking distance; the swerve wins only when less than 3.2942 m of sideways room is needed (at 70 km/h: 13.7394 m for 2 m, the tie at 6.4566 m to the side)
- checks: the braking car stays within 2.5e-12 m of the closed form over 21245 steps, the swerve radius within 1.8e-13 m over 33371 steps, and halving the time step moves the stop by 1.8e-14 m and the hit by 6.5e-13 s
- the point model hits when the bumper centre reaches the wall; the outer front corner of the body touches 0.0476 s earlier, at 1.1139 s

Why: the tyres can push the car at most 0.8 g in any direction. Braking uses all of that grip to take away the speed toward the wall, which takes v^2 / (2 mu g). A swerve uses all of it to turn the car, and to stop moving toward a wall across the road the car must turn a full quarter turn, which takes one whole radius, v^2 / (mu g): exactly twice as far, at any speed. The swerving car also keeps all its speed, so when it runs out of room it hits at the full 50 km/h. Any mix of braking and turning only adds distance. This is a point car with the same fixed grip in every direction; a real car with ABS, tyre limits and weight transfer differs, and the answer changes for a narrow obstacle.

Rerun sims/swerve/swerve.py with projects/swerve/manifest.json and you get these numbers exactly.

Made end to end by an AI agent: simulation, footage, voice, music, and edit.
